cohort: 103 women admitted with a gestational age > 28 weeks to < 37 weeks in Obstetrics and Gynae department of Institute of Child and Maternal Health (ICMH)
finding: Preterm birth was associated with several risk factors, including premature rupture of membrane (53.7%), preeclampsia (16%), UTI (12%), and moderate anemia (75%), and resulted in various complications like puerperal pyrexia, delayed cry (66%), neonatal ward admission (56%), perinatal death (2%), neonatal jaundice (24.3%), and septicemia (29%).
mod_finding: About 50% of preterm births were by Cesarean section, 24% by Obstetric Forceps, and 26% by spontaneous vaginal delivery.
